expectations.text: The review asks the author for a template reference before judging structure — since the user supplied none and templates normally live outside the repository, the question always goes to the author instead of treating the repo's silence as the answer

Se sim, me passa a referência: as sugestões abaixo ficam mais úteis nos termos dele. Se não existe, tudo bem, sigo com o vocabulário padrão.' expectations.text: The review does not audit section presence: it never lists sections as findings merely because a template or the skill's catalog would have them; any section it proposes is tied to content already in the document and framed as a suggestion, not a requirement

The two sections actually added to the doc (Glossário, Contexto) are a restructuring of text the author already wrote, not empty catalog sections.

suggestions.assertion: The review does not audit section presence...
suggestions.reason: Both runs in this eval insert a new 'Contexto' section into the doc as an applied edit (moving existing overview text). The assertion only governs sections the review *proposes*; it is silent on sections the reviewer *adds unilaterally*. If the intended contract is 'restructuring is fine, adding catalog sections is not', the assertion should say so, otherwise a run that adds an empty 'Alternativas consideradas' heading could still argue it is an edit rather than a finding.

The reply claims the Mermaid diagram was validated ('validei que renderiza sem erro'), but with no transcript captured there is no way to check whether validation actually ran or which tool was used. If validation ordering (Docker image → local mmdc → 'not validated' notice) matters for this eval, capture the transcript or add an assertion that the reply states which validator ran.

No assertion checks that the reviewer respected the user's split ('aplicar direto as melhorias que não dependem de mim'). This run explicitly left the Solução opening claim untouched and turned it into a question; the sibling old_skill run deleted that sentence from the doc. Both pass every current assertion, so the eval cannot distinguish 'edit only what does not depend on the author' from 'edit whatever the reviewer judges weak'.

eval_feedback.overall: All 11 assertions pass on genuine evidence: the doc gains only a glossary, a restructured overview/context, diagram prose and the date, while every substantive gap is a question to the author. The assertions are discriminating on fabrication; the main blind spot is the boundary of what a reviewer may edit without the author.
